title: If you fall in: fight the urge to swim
rule: Lie back, spread out and breathe for the first minute.
points: Cold water makes you gasp and panic for about a minute|Lie on your back with your ears in the water|Once your breathing settles, call for help or swim to safety|Then call 911
summary: Cold water shock is what drowns most people in the Hather, not a lack of swimming skill.
body:
Cold water shock is what drowns most people in the Hather, not a lack of swimming skill.

This advice is written for a fictional river. On a real river, follow your local rescue service.

title: The saltmarsh and the tide
rule: Check the tide before you walk out, and turn back early.
points: The flood tide fills the creeks faster than you can walk|Mud below the sea wall can hold you to the knee|Carry a phone in a waterproof pouch|If you are stuck in mud, spread your weight and call 911
summary: Most of our searches start on the marsh path when the tide comes in.
body:
Most of our searches start on the marsh path when the tide comes in.

This advice is written for a fictional river. On a real river, follow your local rescue service.

title: Flood water
rule: Never walk or drive through flood water.
points: Fifteen centimeters of moving water can knock you over|Thirty centimeters can float a car|Manhole covers lift in floods|Follow the county's flood warnings
summary: When the Hather floods, the water on the roads moves faster than it looks.
body:
When the Hather floods, the water on the roads moves faster than it looks.

title: Ice on the mill pond
rule: Stay off the ice, and keep dogs on a lead near it.
points: Pond ice is rarely thick enough to hold a person|If someone goes through, call 911 and do not go out after them|Reach with a branch or a line from the bank
summary: Two of our winter callouts were for dogs through the ice.
body:
Two of our winter callouts were for dogs through the ice.

title: If your dog goes in
rule: Stay on the bank and call 911.
points: Most dogs get out by themselves|Move downstream to where the bank is lower and call them|Never go in after a dog
summary: Owners who go in after their dogs are the people we most often fail to reach in time.
body:
Owners who go in after their dogs are the people we most often fail to reach in time.

title: Paddling and swimming
rule: Wear a buoyancy aid, and tell someone where you are going.
points: Check the tide times and the wind|Carry a phone in a waterproof pouch|Use a quick-release leash on a paddleboard|Stay clear of the weir pool and the Bar
summary: The Hather is a lovely river to paddle, and most trips go fine with a little planning.
body:
